headline: RETAIN SEQUENTIAL EXECUTION. AC9 requires >=1.25x throughput over sequential native execution; the best result anywhere on the grid is 1.11x (size 10000, 8 threads). There is NO crossover size at which threading pays. The cause is measured, not guessed: per-row cost is dominated by the GIL-held snapshot and rebuild phases, so the parallelisable slice is too small for more workers to help. A completed negative experiment with measurements.
not_introduced: no public batch API on any model
no package deployment; the crate remains development-only and is loaded by path
no parallel execution of arbitrary Python callbacks
reproduce: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from benchmarks.native_validation import load_native, parallel_grid; print(parallel_grid(load_native(build=False)))"

safety.bounded_pool: Workers are bounded and reusable: the pool is built once per plan with an explicit count. Asking for 0 threads yields sequential execution rather than Rayon's one-per-core default, so nothing is ever unbounded.
safety.deterministic_order: par_iter().collect() preserves index order regardless of completion order; ineligible rows keep their slot as None. Verified identical to sequential over 30 repeats and under 16-way oversubscription on a 7-row batch.
safety.ineligible_stays_serial: Ineligible rows are never executed natively, never reordered, and are returned as None in their own slot for the caller to run serially.
safety.no_worker_touches_python: Structural, not statistical: rows are snapshotted into owned Rust values with the GIL held, the pool runs inside Python::detach with nothing Python-shaped in scope, and results are rebuilt only after the GIL is re-acquired. A user callback therefore cannot run in a worker -- verified by test_no_callback_runs_during_batch_execution.

amdahl.conclusion: The measured best of 1.11x corresponds to validation being roughly 10% of the work. Reaching AC9's 1.25x would require it to exceed 20%. It does not, and making it so would mean making the boundary cheaper -- which is the same blocker TASK-18 identified, not a threading problem.
